newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil subway privatization moves ahead.
newsitem.headline: Brazil subway privatization moves ahead.

text.p: Up to 30 institutions are applying today to carry out the financial evaluation of Rio de Janeiro's subway Metro which is being privatized next year, the state planning secretary said.
Under the Rio de Janeiro state privatization program, a 20-year concession to run Metro's services will be offered to private investors in May 1997, Marco Aurelio Alencar said.

The state estimates savings of 150 million reais ($150 million) annually by contracting out the running of the trains and their maintenance. The state's responsibility will be to invest in the network to modernize it and improve it.
Alencar said 426 million reais ($426 million) would be invested to construct 13.8 km of new track. Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) is financing 70 percent of the sum.
The subway carries 400,000 passengers daily, but the state aims to increase that number to 1.1 million.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
